ground_truth.title: The Best Cheap Wireless Earbuds under $50 - March 2026
ground_truth.author: Bart Breij
ground_truth.main_content:
Top 5 budget TWS under $50 from Amazon and AliExpress

You don't need to spend much to get wireless earbuds full of great features and stunning sound. These are the best TWS wireless earbuds under 50 dollars, updated for March 2026.

BEST TWS UNDER $50 - March 2026:

Best overall / ANC earbuds - Soundcore P31i / R60i NC

Runner-up - Realme Buds Air7

Best sound quality - Sony WF-C510

Best half-in-ears - Oppo Enco Buds3

Best clip-ons - Baseus Bass BC1 ( NEW )

Best for bass - CMF Buds 2

Extra recommendations:

Best for calls - QCY MeloBuds N70

Money saver - Baseus Bass BP1 Pro

With phone stand - Soundcore P30i

Check out below for descriptions!

How Scarbir.com tests $50 wireless earbuds

Scarbir.com is a one-man job. Since 2019, I've performed all 507+ wireless earphone reviews on this site myself - so you can be sure every model has gotten the same testing methods and the same reference.

I try and test all earbuds at least 1 to 2 weeks fully before writing about it, experiencing all aspects of the earbuds. All earbuds are tested on an Android phone, iPhone, and Mac.

I test the basics like wearing comfort after several hours, the actual battery life, the fit when you're on the move, the controls, and the reliability of the Bluetooth connection. If an earbud fails in any of these categories, it has very little chance to become a recommendation.

For phone and video calls, all earbuds undergo the same tests; recordings performed in the same office and on the same crowded traffic intersection with occasional wind, as well as in pre-defined simulated scenes with noise and wind.

Active Noise Cancelling, if available, is always tested in the same organic office and outdoor environments, as well as in pre-defined simulated background chatter and noise scenarios. ANC performance is always directly compared to the best scoring models in the price range.

The gaming performance and low-latency modes are always tested with the highly challenging shooter Call of Duty mobile on an Android phone.

For the app support of an earbud, I look at the features, the ease-of-use and the needed permissions of the Android and iPhone app.

Sound quality is my biggest passion and, with so much competition on the market, it's what can make or brake an earphone. I listen to earbuds on low, moderate and high active listening volume, take notes and compare an earbud to its biggest comparably priced rivals. Sound performance is both tested by both everyday and active listening to whichever music I throw at it, and by checking technicalities with my Scarbir.com Earbuds Test List on Spotify.

The amount of features on wireless earbuds in the $50 price category varies greatly. That's why earbuds with a bigger amount of useful features (like ANC, app support, and dual-device/ multipoint connection have a fair chance to rank higher than earbuds without. Please read the descriptions in this Buying Guide carefully to see which pair will suit you.

What to expect from truly wireless earphones under $50?

Great build quality: wearing cheap TWS doesn't have to make you feel like a cheapskate. Other than the best earphones under 25 dollars, offerings in this price category often look and feel nice in your ears.

Solid battery life: the battery life of the best earphones in this price range lasts between 5 to 8 hours on a single charge.

More and more functions: as the competition is insane, even $50 earphones offer plenty of features, like app-support with equalizers, dedicated modes for mobile gaming, good call quality, and even Active Noise Cancelling.

Amazing sound quality for the money: the products in this list offer an impeccable sound quality for the amount of money you pay for them. The items listed here have a better, more balanced and cohesive sound than the Apple AirPods and many more capable sounding earphones over 100 dollars.

Has this guide helped you? Please consider supporting my work:

Let's go! Here are the best best cheap true wireless earbuds under $50, updated for March 2026 with a new top recommendation for clip-on earbuds:

1. Best cheap wireless earbuds under $50: Soundcore P31i / R60i NC

All the basics, good ANC, AND great features!

Long battery life, good Active Noise Cancelling, engaging sound, and a baffling amount of great features - including live translation! The Soundcore P31i / R60i NC by Anker is a budget-friendly wireless earphone EVERYONE should consider.

The Soundcore P31i (international name) or Soundcore R60i NC (Indian and Indonesian name) is the successor to the best-selling Soundcore P20i / R50i and it's so much better in every single way. In fact, it's so good, it almost disrupts the entire earphone market.

The earphones rock the basics: they provide a safe and comfortable fit with the diagonal earpieces and oval rubber ear tips. They are IP55 waterproof protected against rain and sweat, and have reliable and completely customizable touch controls near the top of the stems.

What's great, is that they combine good Active Noise Cancelling that filters out constant middle and higher sounds well with a massive 8 hours playtime on a single charge.

That means these last an entire workday or can help you sleep for an entire night.

After that, recharging them in the case for just 10 minutes, grants them 3,5 hours of additional playtime. That's a great fast-charging score in this price range.

The P31i or R60i NC isn't flawless. It handles phone calls and video meetings well as long as there's not too much noise or wind, and it 'only' has a decent Transparency mode to let you hear some traffic when you're playing music.

And even though it has a fluent and immersive gaming sound performance, audio doesn't always sync perfectly with video on Android phones - the earphones' biggest issue.

But what it does in return for this price, is almost insane.

The free Soundcore app for iPhone and Android comes with countless sound customization options, lets you create your own relaxing soundscapes from 62 sound effects and… has an AI assistant that lets you translate meetings or lectures in real-time!

It translates over 100 languages into whatever language you desire, and it works fast and reliable - better than Apple's $250 AirPods Pro 3 or the $100 Realme Buds Air 7 Pro and OnePlus Buds 4, with the translated text read out straight into your ears.

Lastly, the sound is great too. Vocals can be a tad nasal, but the P31i / R60i NC entertains with a tight, deep and 'stabby' bass, pronounced lower mid-tones, and a comfortable treble. As it leaves the mid-tones a bit in the background, it leaves space in the sound too, and instruments and details can flank you on your left and right - whether you listen on background volume or the highest active listening levels.

The Soundcore P31i / R60i NC is almost too good for a pair of wireless earphones under 50 dollars, combining great battery life and comfort with good ANC, entertaining sound and a baffling amount of features.

Soundcore P31i/ R60i NC review

Buy on Amazon US

Buy on your Amazon country

Look up on AliExpress

2. Runner-up for best wireless earbuds under $50: Realme Buds Air 7

These budget earbuds have it all

The Realme Buds Air 7 is another wireless earphone to offer a splendid, complete package under 50 dollars.

There are few highly affordable wireless earbuds that look so polished as the Realme Buds Air 7. This cheaper sibling of the Realme Buds Air 7 Pro has a slick and sturdy metallic charging case, and the earbuds themselves are IP55 water and dust resistant and have unique and flat, square-sided stems.

On the inside, the earbuds have a proven oval shape. The earbuds sit snugly in your ears and are comfortable to wear for hours. Which you can: the Buds Air 7 last a whopping 8 hours on a single charge with Active Noise Cancelling on.

The ANC itself is solid. The Realme takes away nearly all static background sounds and electronic humming. Higher sounds are still audible in traffic and crowded situations, but the Realme can bring rest to your head in a heartbeat.

If you need to hear traffic around you while listening to music, the Transparency mode delivers up to moderate music playback. Wind noise can be reduced by a setting in the free Realme app for iPhone and Android.

The app also lets you customise controls. It's one of the versatile features of this model - just like the dual-device multipoint connection that lets you connect the earbuds to two devices and switch automatically between them.

Playing games is a joy with spot-on synchronisation between audio and video, and phone calls sound loud and clear, even with a bit of wind. Only when there's noise and wind together, your voice can dip a little.

Sound-wise, the Realme Buds Air 7 is big on bass, with heavy and lasting bass tones. Mid-tones sound clear, and while vocals are forward and nuanced, the overall treble is comfortable - there's just more of it than on many of its rivals. If you want to tone down the bass, the Clear Vocals equalizer preset in the app has you covered so well, the Realme Buds Air 7 actually comes recommended for lovers of bass and lovers of a more balanced sound.

That's the story here. The Realme Buds Air 7 is such a great all-around pair, it comes recommended to anyone looking for wireless earphones on a budget.

Realme Buds Air 7 review

Buy on other Amazon countries

3. Best sounding wireless earbuds under $50: Sony WF-C510

great battery life and lots of sound potential

If you're willing to miss out on Active Noise Cancelling, the tiny but mighty Sony WF-C510 treats you with fantastic musical capabilities.

The Sony WF-C510 is Sony's entry-level model of wireless earbuds, and also its smallest model from its lineup. The charging case is compact enough to carry comfortably in any jeans pocket, just like the earbuds are small and comfortable too.

The earbuds have a bit of a pebble-shape, of which the broadest part will point to the back of your ear. Sony cleverly put a little dot on top of the left earbud, so you can easily recognise the top side and separate the left from the right bud. The WF-C510 also comes with very grippy ear tips, to ensure the buds stay in your ears.

This Sony is one of the very few earbuds to boast actual buttons instead of touch panels. You change tracks on the right bud, and decrease or increase the volume by pressing the button on the left or right earbud four times. It's a weird control scheme - but the buttons respond well.

What's more impressive, is the Sony's massive 11 hours playtime on a single charge! The case can recharge the earbuds fully twice before needing new power via USB-C itself.

The WF-C510 also comes with multipoint connection, so you can connect it up to two devices at the same time. It switches to the other device as soon as you start a song or video on it, or when you get a phone call.

It's not advised to bring the C510 outside or in the wind when calling, but a phone call or video meeting in a quieter office room shouldn't be a problem. And if you're into it, the Sony also boasts a great gaming mode, that synchronizes the sounds with the action on your screen greatly. There's no Active Noise Cancelling on these earbuds, however.

Ultimately, it's the sound quality that sets the Sony apart. With one remark: you have to look beyond the balanced and clear, but also bone-dry sound these earbuds have out of the box.

By taking a test in the Sony Connect app for iPhone or Android and choosing which of the given fragments sounds best to you, the WF-C510 prepares a custom equalizer for you. That's a great starting point for further custom equalisation, which is easy to do and has a proper impact on the sound.

Sony gives you all the tools to create an engaging sound with a tightly kicking bass, powerful vocals and a wonderful, airy treble. Mid-tones like guitars and piano play sound uniquely natural in this price range, instruments are textured, and it's easy to hear nuances like breath grasps and the plucking of strings in higher quality recordings.

Check out the equalizer screenshot in my review to see how I got the Sony WF-C510 to be the best sounding earbuds under 50 dollars.

The Sony WF-C510 may not look like the best deal with its missing Active Noise Cancelling, but the battery life, comfort and especially the sound quality are outstanding in this price range.

Sony WF-C510 review

Buy on Amazon US

Buy on your Amazon country

4. Best half-in-ear earbuds under $50: Oppo Enco Buds3

Incredible battery, multipoint, and good sound

Prefer your wireless earbuds without rubber tips? The Oppo Enco Buds3 combines amazing battery life, good wearing comfort, clear calls, and comfortable sound well under 50 dollars.

The Oppo Enco Buds3 is the followup to the Oppo Enco Air3 that was the top recommendation in this Buying Guide for over a year. With the Air3 now out of production, it's good to know that the successor is just as good - and comes in an even smaller if scratchy charging case.

The Enco Buds3 has a small speaker mound, reminiscent of the earlier AirPods models instead of the AirPods 4, and it provides a snug and secure fit, as well as good wearing comfort. That's a great combination with the IP54 waterproof rating against rain and sweat - meaning you can take these out for a run or a workout.

Operating them is a breeze too. The touch panels on top of the earbuds respond quickly and with clicky feedback. Definitely change the controls from the free HeyMelody app on iPhone or Android, though, as the standard controls don't even have a button for play/pause.

The most surprising part of this budget half-in-ear earphone is its battery life: the Enco Buds3 plays up to 9 hours on a single charge. It can easily last an entire workday or night.

It doesn't matter what you do with the earbuds during that time: it nails every task.

You can connect them to two devices at the same time with the dual-device multipoint connection, and the earbuds switch automatically when you enter a call.

Phone and video calls are clear, as the microphones put your voice through natural and full. Noise around you is filtered well and doesn't drown your voice. It even survives a bit of wind. The gaming mode is equally convincing, with the sound effects synchronizing the action on a challenging game like Call of Duty mobile perfectly.

Lastly, the Oppo Enco Buds3 sounds good too. These are some of the fullest, smoothest sounding half-in-ears you can get on a small budget. It offers steady mid-bass thumps, a subtly rumbling sub-bass, boosted lower-mid tones that give the music warmth, and full-bodied vocals.

If you already had or have the Oppo Enco Air3, you may miss the boost in the mid-tones that accentuated guitar and piano play, but the Buds3 pleases with its warm and comforting sound.

The Oppo Enco Buds3 are affordable half-in-ears you can wear all day or night due to its fantastic battery life - and succeed in every task you throw at them.

Oppo Enco Buds 3 review

Buy on Amazon

Buy on AliExpress

5. Best open-ear clip-on earbuds under $50: Baseus Bass BC1

Low cost, high quality

In the young market of clip-on earbuds, many models make simple mistakes or sound rather bad. The Baseus Bass BC1 is a genius exception. For as little as 20 to 40 dollars, these clip-on earbuds do everything right.

If you're looking for cheap earbuds that allow to completely hear your surroundings while listening to music, look no further than this Baseus.

The Bass BC1 has a solid battery life of 7 hours playtime on a single charge, and its round charging case packs 4 full recharges before it needs new power via USB-C. You'll have plenty of battery with you.

The Bass BC1 consists of a small round part in your ears and a slightly larger square behind your ear. You can feel it a bit as it presses lightly. Yet, these earbuds offer enough comfort to wear for hours and a stable enough fit for runs and workouts - which are also secured by the IP55 waterproof rating against rain and sweat.

The actual button on top of the square behind your ears also helps operating these earbuds when you're on the move, although you can move the earphones a bit when using them.

What's more, is that you can fully customize the controls with the Baseus app for iPhone and Android, including volume controls.

In phone calls, your voice can appear a bit thin, but it actually holds well when there's noise around you, and even a tiny bit of wind. The default Bluetooth connectivity is good too, and you can connect them to two devices with the multipoint connection.

When it comes to sound, the BC1 has a high maximum volume and also convinces with great reproduction of lower frequencies, which is quite rare for clip-ons.

The mid-bass has a decent slam and a bit of fulness, and darker electronic tones, guitar and piano play have a natural weight. In fact, the earphones can sound a bit too low-focused out of the box.

That's where the Hi-Fi Live sound preset from the Baseus app comes in, that leaves the lows intact, while opening up the treble in a gentle and comfortable way.

It makes room for higher outbursts while controlling them, and it also has lovely deep male vocals in songs, audio books and podcasts. That combination is rare for this type of earphones.

Last but not least, video playback is flawless and the earphones also sync sound effects well with the action on your screen in games. It's pretty much an earphone for all your tasks, except maybe for transit purposes, as the sound leakage is a bit higher than average.

The Baseus Bass BC1 is a great all-around, dirt cheap pair of clip-on earbuds with actual buttons, plenty of battery, decent phone calls, and good sound.

Baseus Bass BC1 vs other cheap clip-ons tested

6. Best bass earbuds under $50: CMF Buds 2

Nothing's budget earbuds are brilliantly bassy

The CMF Buds 2 by Nothing are the best budget earbuds for bass lovers. These funky looking earphones can be pushed to extremes.

Nothing could well be the hottest tech brand when it comes to design these days, along with its budget lineup of CMF products. The CMF Buds 2 come in a funky, rounded square charging case with a dial you can attach a strap onto. They're available in black and white, but also bright red or this mint green - in which it surely draws attention.

The sleek design continues on in the Nothing X app for iPhone and Android, that lets you customise the responsive touch controls, activate the well-performing gaming mode, or let you alter the sound.

The question is: how do you want that sound to be? Warm, smooth, and bassy? Or BASSY?

With the Ultra Bass-slider within the app, you can actively lift the volume of the bass, which already provides big, fat, deep sub-bass rumbles and heavy mid-bass thumps out of itself.

Other than bass, the CMF Buds 2 boosts the lower mid-tones, and gives vocals a warm and even thick vibe. You should look elsewhere for a clear sound (although you can lift treble nicely with the Classical equalizer), but the CMF Buds 2 entertains with good instrumental separation and some nice left-right detailing in the sound.

Looking beyond sound, the CMF Buds 2 lasts 6,5 hours on a single charge, has an IP55 waterproof rating, and comes with decent Active Noise Cancelling. It's great to reduce constant sounds, but doesn't reduce sudden sounds as well as the QCY MeloBuds Pro. It does, however, leave out wind noise wonderfully.

In phone calls and video meetings, your surroundings are left out of the call, and you can also connect the CMF Buds 2 to two devices at the same time. It's a wonderful alternative to the MeloBuds Pro if you prefer a smoother and warmer sound.

Check my review to see how the CMF Buds 2 compares to the CMF Buds Pro 2.

If you're looking for the biggest bass on a budget, look nu further than the CMF Buds 2.

Honourable mentions for best TWS under $50:

Best for phone calls: QCY MeloBuds N70

The QCY MeloBuds N70 are more fantastic wireless earphones on a budget, and offer above-average call clarity both indoors and outside.

The QCY doesn't reduce the most background noise during phone calls and video meetings, but it always keeps priority on your voice. Even in noisy circumstances or in wind, your voice stays stable and clear.

There's more to these earphones. They last 7 hours on a single charge and they bring solid Active Noise Cancelling too - although slightly less effective than the Soundcore P31i and Realme Buds Air 7. Video and gaming playback is great, and the earphones are IPX5 waterproof protected against rain and sweat.

The sound leans a little on lower tones and it can be a bit darker as a result, but with the Spatial Audio option in the QCY app, the MeloBuds N70 can sound big and theatrical - with details around you and lovely vocal nuances.

The QCY MeloBuds N70 is definitely one of the best earphones under $50, and especially worth looking into when you regularly take phone or video calls.

QCY MeloBuds N70 review

$35 to $60 - Buy on Amazon, your Amazon country or AliExpress

Best for saving money: Baseus Bass BP1 Pro

The Baseus Bass BP1 Pro, also sold as Baseus EP10 Pro, is a great option of you're looking for a fun sound and good ANC on a budget. You can save some money too - these cost around 25 dollars.

These earbuds sound BIG - and bathe you with warmth. The downside is that vocals are less clear; it doesn't sound as vibrant in treble heavy genres.

The BP1 Pro has a big charging case, but its earbuds deliver 7,5 hours of playtime on a single charge, and that's with its convincing Active Noise Cancelling on. Your voice sound use a bit more volume in calls, however.

Baseus Bass BP1 Pro review

$25 to $40 - See price on Amazon US, your Amazon country or AliExpress

With phone stand: Soundcore P30i

If you love your music with a strong bass, the Soundcore P30i is a great alternative to the CMF Buds. It has an even tighter and fiercer mid-bass kick than the CMF. The CMF can be pushed to bigger extremes, however, and sounds a bit more articulated as well.

Don't rule the Soundcore P30i out, though! These earbuds have 7 hours battery life on a single charge, get support from the fantastic Soundcore app that also provide customisable controls, and… its charging case has an extra lid that acts as a phone stand. A function that's brilliantly convenient if you watch a movie in a train, or play a game with friends every now and then.

Soundcore P30i review

$30 to $50 - Buy on Amazon US or your Amazon country

And even though it has a fluent and **immersive gaming sound performance**, audio doesn't always sync perfectly with video on Android phones - the earphones' biggest issue.

But **what it does in return for this price, is almost insane**.

The free Soundcore app for iPhone and Android comes with **countless sound customization options**, lets you create your own relaxing soundscapes from 62 sound effects and… has an **AI assistant that lets you translate meetings or lectures in real-time**!

**The Soundcore P31i / R60i NC is almost too good for a pair of wireless earphones under 50 dollars, combining great battery life and comfort with good ANC, entertaining sound and a baffling amount of features.**
